about: PEOPLE OF WEIGHT AND PILLARS (Design/fate_faith_and_self.md section 6d), for the first life, 793 to about 805. Written 7 Oct 2026. 'people' are the kings, queens, bishops, abbots, counts and reeves alive in those years whom a merchant of the twelve ports (dorestad, traiectum, walichrum, lundenwic, witla, medemelacha, doccinga, daventre, quentovic, sarre, fordwic, ripa) could meet, hear of daily, or be ruined by. Each has an id (wt.<name>), the cast and places ids where the person is already written (Design/content/spine.json, Data/places/<port>.json), office, dates, a seat (a port id of ports_793.json), 'reach' (twelve: met in a port of the first release; dim: sits in a port outside it; word: known only by news), traits, a temper at the start and what moves it, what holds them up (two or three bonds, by person id where the bond is a person, in plain words where it is God, a name or a house), and what they carry (the ids of hours in hours_793.json and of entries in chronicle_793.json that rest on them). A temper is one of: steady, grieving, hardened, broken, vengeful, exalted. 'historical' false means the person is the game's own in a real office. Everything said of a real person's character beyond the source line is the game's reading. 'pillars' are the events: for each, the named things it stands on, a spare pillar where history is heavy (knock one out and it still stands, a little bent), and its plain, bent and fallen outcomes, each a chronicle line in the flat voice of the Anglo-Saxon Chronicle and a list of what it does: 'effects' in the engine's verbs with the port named (Effects.cs: price_shock, news, flag), 'people' whose temper moves, and 'words' for the rest. SCOPE: chronicle_793.json has about 230 entries for 793 to 805, most of them far away (Baghdad, Constantinople, Spain, Ireland). Pillars are written here for the entries that touch the twelve ports, their realms and these people, and for every hour of hours_793.json; every other entry stands by the rule under 'far_events'. (?) marks what could not be checked; LATER a source written long after. Chronicle lines are our own plain words. A draft for the user to overwrite.

tempers.grieving: slow to act, generous to the church, easier to move by Troth and harder by Tongue
tempers.hardened: acts sooner and harsher than the record; resists Tongue and Name one step more
tempers.broken: does not act; what rests on them falls unless a spare pillar holds
tempers.vengeful: acts against one person or people beyond reason; resists Nerve one step less (a firm word turns them), and remembers
tempers.exalted: over-reaches; resists Lore one step less (flattered by learning) and Nerve one step more

far_events.rule: An entry of chronicle_793.json with no pillar here stands on nothing the player can reach. It fires on its day as news, with the effect the chronicle and shocks_793.json already give it. If a person of weight it names is dead or broken by the player's doing before its day, it is skipped and the log prints: 'Of this the book says nothing in your world.'
far_events.source: Design/fate_faith_and_self.md section 6d ('events with no written line fall back to a plain rule')

people.name: Charles
people.office: king of the Franks and Lombards; emperor from 25 December 800
people.seat_note: no fixed seat; winters at Aachen from 794; the palace above the Waal at Noviomagus is the nearest to the twelve
people.reach: twelve, once: at Quentovic and Saint-Riquier, March to April 800; otherwise word
people.traits: Tall, loud and cheerful; talks more than a king should; plain Frankish dress; loves strangers, swimming, roast meat and learning; cannot bear a fast or a doctor.

temper.why: 792 and 793 are his worst years: his eldest son's plot, famine, the Saxons and Frisians risen, a count's host wiped out by the Weser, the canal lost to rain.

moves.by: queen Fastrada dies
the Avars beaten and their treasure brought home
queen Liutgard dies; he does not marry again
crowned emperor
Alcuin dies

people.source: Einhard, Vita Karoli c. 18-25; ARF 792-814; chronicle_793.json

people.name: Charles the Younger
people.office: the king's eldest son by Hildegard; leads the hosts in Saxony and against the Slavs; anointed king on Christmas Day 800
people.seat_note: with the host
people.traits: His father's right hand in war. It was for him that a daughter of Offa was asked, about 789, and from Offa's answer that the ports were shut.

people.name: Fastrada
people.office: queen of the Franks
people.seat_note: with the court
people.traits: Einhard lays two plots against the king at the door of her cruelty. He wrote thirty years on, and of a dead woman.

temper.why: Einhard's word for her, not ours

people.name: Liutgard
people.office: queen of the Franks
people.dates: married about 794 to 796; died 4 June 800 at Tours
people.seat_note: with the court; on the coast with the king in spring 800
people.traits: Young, bookish, praised by every poet at court; Alcuin's friend. No children.

people.name: Alcuin
people.office: deacon of York; master at the king's court; abbot of Saint Martin's at Tours from 796
people.seat_note: at court, not in a port; the cell of Saint Josse by Quentovic is said to be his from about 792 (?)
people.reach: twelve, by the game's own meeting; otherwise by letter
people.traits: Warm and wordy; scolds those he loves; a nickname for everyone; cannot leave a riddle alone.

temper.why: From June 793 he writes of nothing but Northumbria: the blood on the altar, the sins that earned it.

moves.by: king Aethelred of Northumbria is murdered; Alcuin gives up going home
given Saint Martin's at Tours

people.name: Gervold
people.office: abbot of Saint-Wandrille; the king's procurator, who takes the tolls at Quentovic
people.traits: A manager and a go-between; many times envoy to Offa, and his friend; likes a thing settled.

moves.by: Offa dies
the tolls go on

people.name: Angilbert
people.office: abbot of Saint-Riquier (Centula); the king's envoy to Rome in 792, 794 and 796
people.seat_note: Saint-Riquier is a day's ride south of Quentovic, which is its port
people.traits: The court's 'Homer': a poet, a builder with three hundred monks under new roofs, and father of two sons by the king's daughter Bertha.

temper.why: He is rebuilding his abbey on a scale no one north of the Alps has seen.

people.source: Nithard, Historiae IV.5; ARF 792, 796, 800; Hariulf, Chronicon Centulense (11th century: LATER) (?)

people.name: Hildebold
people.office: bishop, then archbishop of Cologne; the king's chief chaplain
people.traits: The churchman nearest the king. Traiectum answers to him.
carries: the bishop of Traiectum's orders in hunger_805

people.name: Hamacar
people.office: bishop of Traiectum
people.traits: Only the name and the years are real. Here: old, careful, with a full barn and a list of the poor.

moves.by: the hunger

people.source: the list of the bishops of Utrecht; Design/content/spine.json

people.name: Liudger
people.office: priest and teacher of the East Frisians; bishop at Mimigernaford from 30 March 805
people.seat_note: Doccinga in 793 to 794; east of the Lauwers after; Werden from about 799
people.traits: A Frisian of good kin, taught at Traiectum and York; gentle, bookish, stubborn about going back.

moves.by: his churches burn
he is back among them

people.name: Folcbert
people.office: count over the Dorestat district
people.traits: The game's creditor: no count, reeve or toll man of Dorestat is named in any source. As written in the cast.

moves.by: his steward is named before the emperor's envoys
the king's envoy speaks for the house

people.name: Wlemar
people.office: one of the two wise men whose judgements are added to the Law of the Frisians
people.seat_note: where he sat is not known (?)
people.traits: Only the name is real. Here: an old law-sayer who distrusts ink.

people.name: Isaac
people.office: 'Isaac the Jew', the king's envoy to the caliph
people.seat_note: on the road
people.traits: The one of three who came back. Tired, exact, hard to surprise.

people.name: Godescalc
people.office: an envoy of king Charles to the king of the Danes
people.seat_note: passing through, by the game's guess (?)
people.traits: Only the name, the errand and the death are real.

people.name: Offa
people.office: king of the Mercians, and lord of every kingdom south of the Humber
people.seat_note: his hall is at Tamworth; Lundenwic is his port, and his councils sit at Chelsea, two miles up the river
people.traits: Forty years a king. A reformer of coin and a giver to churches, who answers a slight from the greatest king in the west by shutting his ports.

temper.why: He is old and has one son. Alcuin wrote afterwards of the blood the father shed to make the kingdom safe for him.

moves.by: a king he sent for did not come

people.name: Cynethryth
people.office: queen of the Mercians; after 796 abbess of Cookham on the Thames
people.seat_note: with the court; pennies were struck in her name at Canterbury by the moneyer Eoba
people.traits: The only English queen with her face on a penny. Alcuin calls her the steward of the king's house and tells her son to learn mercy from her. The tale that she plotted king Aethelberht's death is of the 12th century.

moves.by: Offa dies
her son dies after 141 days
she keeps Cookham by a bargain with the archbishop

people.source: her pennies; Alcuin, letters 61, 62 (?); the record of the synod of Clofesho, 798 (S 1258)

people.name: Ecgfrith
people.office: king of the Mercians, hallowed in 787 beside his father
people.seat_note: Tamworth
people.traits: Nine years a king-in-waiting, 141 days a king.

people.name: Cenwulf
people.office: king of the Mercians
people.seat_note: Tamworth; his minster at Winchcombe
people.traits: Writes to the pope with great humility and maims a rival the same year. Careful of rank; argues from old books.

temper.why: He takes a kingdom whose two richest provinces have just thrown it off.

moves.by: Kent is his again and his brother is its king

people.source: Anglo-Saxon Chronicle (A, F) 796; Cenwulf and Leo III, letters of 798

people.name: Cuthred
people.office: king of Kent, Cenwulf's brother
people.seat_note: Canterbury, a mile up the track from the hythe
people.traits: Known from his pennies and his charters. Here: a quiet man set over people who hate his brother.

people.name: Eadberht, called Praen
people.office: a priest who left his orders; king of the Kentish people
people.seat_note: Canterbury
people.traits: Bold, quick, short of friends. The pope calls him an apostate cleric.

temper.why: an exile from a kingdom Offa swallowed

moves.by: Kent takes him for king
blinded and his hands cut off

people.source: Anglo-Saxon Chronicle (A, F) 794, 796; Leo III to Cenwulf, 798

people.name: Aethelheard
people.office: archbishop of Canterbury
people.seat_note: Canterbury
people.traits: A Mercian abbot set over Kent by Offa. Ran when Kent rose; went to Rome to win back by letters what force had taken.

moves.by: he flees his church
he is brought home behind a Mercian host
Canterbury has the whole south again

people.source: Anglo-Saxon Chronicle (A) 799, 803; Alcuin's letters to him; en.wikipedia.org 'Aethelhard' for the day of his enthroning

people.name: Wulfred
people.office: archdeacon of Canterbury; archbishop from 805
people.seat_note: Canterbury
people.traits: Rich in his own right, a rebuilder, and in time the one man in England who will not give way to Cenwulf.

people.name: Selethryth
people.office: abbess of Lyminge, and holder of the minster on Thanet (?)
people.seat_note: the abbess of Thanet has her own ships toll-free at Sarre and Fordwic; that Selethryth held Thanet as well as Lyminge is likely, not sure (?)
people.traits: Sister of a king's thegn, Ealdberht. In 804 she asks for, and gets, a plot inside the walls of Canterbury as a refuge for her women: she can see what is coming by sea.

moves.by: Kent is laid waste round her house

holds_up: the kings' charters (wt.offa, then wt.cenwulf and wt.cuthred)
people.source: S 125 (786); S 160 (804); the Kentish toll charters for Thanet. The places file has a later abbess, Cwenthryth (sarre.cwenthryth), Cenwulf's daughter, for the 820s.

people.name: Aethelberht
people.office: king of the East Angles
people.seat_note: where he sat is not known
people.reach: twelve, once: on his road, by the game's guess
people.traits: Known in his own time only by his pennies, with his name as king and the wolf and twins.
holds_up: his own penny (his name as king)

people.name: Eadwald
people.office: king of the East Angles
people.traits: Known only from his pennies.

people.name: Beorhtric
people.office: king of the West Saxons, Offa's son-in-law
people.seat_note: Winchester
people.traits: A king by Offa's leave. It was to his reeve that the first three ships of Northmen came, and killed him.

moves.by: his protector dies and the exile over the sea is still alive

people.name: Eadburh
people.office: daughter of Offa; queen of the West Saxons from 789
people.seat_note: Winchester; at Quentovic once, in 802, by the game's guess
people.traits: As her enemies told it ninety years on: her father's daughter, used to ruling, quick to hate.

moves.by: her father dies
her husband dies and she runs

people.name: Ecgberht
people.office: an exile of the West Saxon royal kin; king of the West Saxons from 802
people.seat_note: in Francia, by the king's leave; where is not recorded (?)
people.traits: Years on another king's bread. Patient, unforgiving, exact about debts.

temper.why: driven out by Offa and Beorhtric

moves.by: he has his kingdom

people.name: Heathoberht
people.office: bishop of London
people.seat_note: Saint Paul's in the old walled city
people.traits: Only the name and the death are real. Here: a tired man with a burned town.

moves.by: the fire

people.source: Historia regum 801. His predecessor Eadbald 'left the land' in 796 (Anglo-Saxon Chronicle (D, E) 794).

people.name: Wighelm
people.office: the king's wic-reeve of Lundenwic
people.dates: born about 750; reeve under Offa and Cenwulf
people.traits: The game's own man in a real office. As written in the cast.

moves.by: his king is dead and the wic is full of strangers

people.name: Sigfred
people.office: king of the Danes
people.seat_note: where he sat is not known; his men are at Ripa in the market weeks, by the game's guess (?)
people.traits: Sheltered the Saxon leader Widukind, and sent envoys to Charles all the same. A king who keeps both doors open.

people.name: Godfred
people.office: king of the Danes
people.seat_note: his fleet and horsemen gather there in 804 and 808
people.reach: dim; through his men at Ripa from 804
people.traits: As the Franks tell it: swollen with empty hope, counting Frisia and Saxony his own.

moves.by: a Dane who has seen the emperor's court tells him what it is

people.name: Thrasco
people.office: prince of the Abodrites
people.traits: The emperor's ally against the Saxons, paid in their land.

temper.why: his predecessor Witzan was killed by Saxons in 795

moves.by: he beats the Saxons beyond the Elbe at Bornhoved

people.name: Leo III
people.office: pope
people.seat_note: Rome
people.traits: Set upon in the street by his predecessor's kin in 799, and carried back to Rome by Frankish spears.

moves.by: attacked in the Greater Litany procession
he crowns an emperor

people.name: Higbald
people.office: bishop of Lindisfarne
people.traits: The man the letters of 793 are written to. He stayed on the island.
holds_up: Saint Cuthbert's body, which was not touched
people.source: Alcuin, letter 20; Symeon, Libellus de exordio II.5

stands_on: no grain to be had from over the sea: the English ports are half shut

plain.line: 793. In this year there was a great hunger in Francia, and men saw false corn standing in the fields that could be touched and not eaten.

does.words: As the chronicle and shocks_793.json already have it.

bent.line: 793. In this year there was a great hunger in Francia; but grain came by ship to the Rhine mouth, and there fewer died.

does.words: A port the player feeds is bent, one at a time.

pillars.source: Annales Laureshamenses 793; Annales Mosellani 792 (=793); thread hungry_years

stands_on: a fleet out of the north that no one knew could cross the open sea
pillars.spare: News is as old as the ship that brings it: no warning can outrun the fleet.

plain.line: 793. In this year dreadful signs came over the land of the Northumbrians: sheets of light, whirlwinds, and fiery dragons seen in the sky. A great hunger followed; and on the sixth day before the Ides of June the harrying of heathen men destroyed God's church on Lindisfarne.

does.words: From now a Northman's speech frightens an English port (self_793.json, the Dane's greetings).

pillars.why_no_fall: It is the first card of the age and falls before the player can know of it. If the game begins on 1 May 793 (fate, section 6b) the player is trading when it happens and hears two weeks later.
pillars.source: Anglo-Saxon Chronicle (D, E) 793; the day from the Lindisfarne annals (the Chronicle's 'January' is a slip)

stands_on: wt.charles far off at Regensburg, so that nothing is done

plain.line: (The book says nothing of the boys again.)

does.words: Silence.

bent.line: 794. One of the boys taken from Lindisfarne came home over the sea in a ship of {house}.

does.words: cast.tidwine lives as a free man.

pillars.why_no_fall: To bring them all home the king would have to treat with the Danes' king for them, and he is a year's ride away.

stands_on: baptism and the tithe laid on by force
the leaders of the rising east of the Lauwers
pillars.spare: The count's men hold the west bank of the Lauwers: the rising does not cross it.

plain.line: 793. In this year the Saxons broke faith again, and the East Frisians with them; churches were burned and the priests driven out.

does.words: No priest east of the Lauwers for a year.

bent.line: 794. Liudger came again among the Frisians before the year was out, and children were baptised who would have died heathen.

does.words: One church east of the river is not burned; its priest remembers the house.

fallen.line: 793. In this year the East Frisians burned their churches, and came over the Lauwers, and burned the church at Doccinga where the holy Boniface was killed.

does.words: Falls only if the player, as a keeper of the old gods, carries word west to east of where the count's men are thin. The feast of 5 June is not kept at Doccinga for three years.

pillars.source: ARF (revised) 793; Altfrid, Vita Liudgeri I.22; Alcuin, letters 107, 110 (the tithe has undone the Saxons' faith)

stands_on: the moneyers of Lundenwic and Canterbury (lundenwic.moneyer, fordwic.eoba)
silver coming in from the Frankish side

plain.line: 793. In this year king Offa had a heavier and broader penny struck, and the old was not taken.

does.words: Old light pennies pass in English ports at a tenth less.

bent.line: 793. In this year king Offa had a heavier penny struck; but silver was short while the Frankish shore was shut, and the old ran beside the new for three years.

does.words: While flag bs_peace is not set.

stands_on: the East Angles have no king ready in his place
pillars.spare: Offa's host can take the East Angles whether their king comes or not.

plain.line: 794. In this year Offa, king of the Mercians, had the head of king Aethelberht struck off.

does.words: The East Angles are Offa's until he dies.

bent.line: 794. In this year Offa had king Aethelberht's head struck off. But the East Angles took Eadwald for king and held their land.

does.words: Two pillars are still up (the king rode, Offa hardened), one is down (an heir was ready).

fallen.line: 794. In this year king Aethelberht was bidden to Offa's hall and did not go. (Here the book leaves the world you know.)

does.words: Re-read in date order: 796-eadwald-east-anglia does not fire; when Offa dies the East Angles are already their own. A Mercian host on the East Anglian border in 795 is a plain rule: grain and horses dear at Lundenwic that summer.

stands_on: wt.charles at Frankfurt with the bishops
pillars.spare: The king sells his own grain below the price he sets: a count who will not keep the law is undersold.

plain.line: 794. In this year the king held a great meeting at Frankfurt, and set what might be asked for a measure of oats, of barley, of rye and of wheat, whether the year were lean or fat; and made one measure for the whole realm, and one penny.

does.words: The most for a new measure: oats one penny, barley two, rye three, wheat four. The new penny must be taken in every market.

bent.line: 794. In this year the king set the price of grain; but in the ports men sold as they could.

does.words: In a port where the count is away with the host and the player has sold dear and been seen.

pillars.source: MGH Capit. I no. 28 c. 4-5; chronicle_793.json 794-06-frankfurt-new-denier

stands_on: a second fleet, come for a second rich house
pillars.spare: The storm does what the brothers could not.

plain.line: 794. In this year the heathen plundered Ecgfrith's minster at the Don mouth; and one of their leaders was killed there, and a storm broke their ships, and many drowned.

does.words: For a year the English say God has answered.

bent.line: 794. In this year the heathen came to Ecgfrith's minster at the Don mouth and found it warned, and took little.

plain.line: 794. In this year queen Fastrada died at Frankfurt and was buried at Saint Alban's by Mainz.

stands_on: wt.charles willing to be Offa's 'brother' again

stands_on: a Mercian archbishop the Kentish do not love

plain.line: (The book does not name him; only his pennies do.)

does.words: The second fire in four years. The widow's ghost ends in it (self_793.json).

pillars.spare: Alcuin had already written the answer everyone could live with: let Lichfield's archbishop keep his cloak for life, and no successor.

plain.line: 803. In this year, on the fourth day before the Ides of October, a council sat at Clofesho, and it was decreed that the seat of an archbishop should never again be at Lichfield, nor anywhere but at Canterbury.

does.words: Canterbury's pilgrims, courts and letters are those of the whole south again: Fordwic's market grows a step.

bent.line: 805. In this year archbishop Aethelheard died; and the matter of Lichfield was ended under Wulfred, who came after him.

does.words: If the crossing was slow or the archbishop reached Rome in winter: two years late.

fallen.line: 801. In this year archbishop Aethelheard was lost in the sea on his way to Rome. (Here the book leaves the world you know.) And the Mercians kept their own archbishop.

does.words: Falls only if the player carries him and the ship is lost. It counts as the life's one Turn. Fordwic's market shrinks a step; the house that drowned an archbishop is not forgiven in Kent.

pillars.source: Leo III to Aethelheard, 18 January 802; Acts of Clofesho 803; Alcuin's letters of 797 to 801

stands_on: the West Saxon great men willing
pillars.spare: He is the only one of the royal kin left alive and of age.

plain.line: 802. In this year king Beorhtric died, and Ecgberht took the kingdom of the West Saxons; and the same day ealdorman Aethelmund rode over at Kempsford, and both ealdormen were killed, and the men of Wiltshire had the victory.

does.words: Mercia has lost its tame king in the south.

bent.line: 802. In this year Ecgberht took the kingdom of the West Saxons. He came home over the sea in a ship of {house}.

does.words: Not for the first release.

stands_on: the West Saxons' hatred of her

plain.line: 802. In this year the queen went over the sea with great treasure to the emperor.

does.words: As Asser tells it she loses everything within a few years.

bent.line: 802. In this year the queen went over the sea to the emperor, who gave her a great house of nuns to rule; and she kept it.

stands_on: his envoys sent out through the realm

plain.line: 802. In this year the emperor had every free man of twelve years and over swear to him as emperor the faith he had sworn to him as king.

does.words: A Frankish, Frisian or Saxon player swears at the count's court, by the form of his faith: a card. A keeper of the old gods who is the emperor's subject must swear on relics or be known. The envoys also hear complaints against counts' men (the clerk's ghost).

stands_on: wt.wlemar and Saxmund, who know the custom
a clerk who can write Frisian words in Latin letters

plain.line: 802. In this year the emperor had the laws of all his peoples read out and written, each man's own.

does.words: From now a suit in a Frisian port is judged by a book.

bent.line: 802. In this year the law of the Frisians was written; and one judgement in it was spoken by a shipman of {house}.

does.words: The book's one changed line.

plain.line: 803. In this year it was ordered that no arm-rings or mail-coats be given to merchants, and that measures be equal everywhere.

does.words: A hold with byrnies in it is seized at any Frankish toll (the engine's 'law seizure'). They are worth half as much again at Ripa.

stands_on: wt.charles with the host at Hollenstedt
the Saxons beyond the Elbe beaten since 798
wt.thrasco ready to take the land
pillars.spare: It is the thirty-third year of the war and nobody is left to stop it.

plain.line: 804. In this year the emperor carried off all the Saxons who lived beyond the Elbe, with their wives and children, into Francia, and gave their land to the Abodrites.

does.words: The host's ground at Daventre is used for the last time. The crew's Brunger learns where his kin were sent, or does not.

bent.line: 804. In this year the emperor carried off the Saxons from beyond the Elbe; and some who fled came to the Danes by sea.

stands_on: the counsel of his men, who do not trust the emperor
the fugitives each king wants from the other
pillars.spare: Neither king can afford to be seen to come to the other.

plain.line: 804. In this year Godfred, king of the Danes, came with his fleet and all the horsemen of his kingdom to Sliesthorp. He had promised to come and speak with the emperor, and did not.

does.words: A Frank is watched at Ripa from now. The road runs on to Reric in 808 and the hundred pounds of 810.

bent.line: 804. In this year Godfred, king of the Danes, came to Sliesthorp, and the kings dealt through envoys, and gave back each other's runaways, and there was peace on the border for a time.

does.words: Stands if two of three hold: Godescalc lived (hr_godescalc_nudge), a Dane who has seen the emperor spoke to the king, the count had a true count of the fleet (gf_warned). The next life opens with Reric still standing in 808, or falling a year later.

pillars.why_no_fall: A meeting of the two kings face to face would be a Turn, and belongs to the second life.

plain.line: 804. In this year Alcuin the deacon died at Tours, on the day of Pentecost.

does.words: The letters stop: the deed carried_letters is worth less on the Channel from now. 19 May 804 was Pentecost by the reckoning in calendar_793.json.

plain.line: 805. In this year archbishop Aethelheard died, and Wulfred was chosen in his place.

does.words: His letter under seal (an heirloom) dies with him.

stands_on: the law that no food leave the realm
counts and bishops who keep it

plain.line: 805. In this year there was a great hunger in many places; and the emperor forbade that any food be sold out of his realm, and set what might be asked for it within.

does.words: Grain may be sold at the cap or run abroad at a great price and a great risk.

bent.line: 806. In the hungry year ships came with grain to the Rhine mouth and sold it at the emperor's price, and it was remembered.

does.words: Port by port.

pillars.source: MGH Capit. I no. 44 c. 4; no. 46 c. 17-18

stands_on: the complaints his envoys brought home

plain.line: 805. In this year it was ordered that only the old and just tolls be taken, at bridges and ships and markets, and no new ones; and that no arms be sold to the Slavs, and that coin be struck nowhere but at the palace.

does.words: A new toll laid on the house since 793 can be challenged at the count's court. Whether the mints at Dorestat and Quentovic truly stopped is doubtful (?): the game keeps them, striking 'by the palace's leave'.
